**Core settings**

| Setting | What it is | Values | Default | When to change it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `candleInterval`<br/>Candle Interval | Candle interval the strategy reads for its EMA cross. | `1m`, `5m`, `15m`, `30m`, `1h`, `4h`, `1d` | `1h` | Set it once, up front. Shorten it if the strategy is missing moves that are over before it reacts; lengthen it if it is entering on noise. | Every other candle-counted setting here (EMA periods, ATR period, trend period) is measured in candles of this interval, so changing it silently rescales all of them. A 200-period trend filter is 200 hours on `1h` and 200 days on `1d`. |
| `trailingStopPct`<br/>Trailing-stop distance (from peak) | How far price may fall from its peak before the trailing-stop sells. 5 means sell on a 5% pullback from the high reached since entry. Must be above 0 and below 100. | text | `0.05` | Widen it if you are being stopped out of trades that then continue up. Tighten it if winners keep giving back most of their gain. | This is the only exit the strategy has by default: the position sells once price falls this far from its highest point since entry. Too tight and normal wobble ends every trade; too wide and a full round trip can end flat. |
| `entryMarginPct`<br/>Entry Margin Pct | How far the fast EMA must exceed the slow EMA to confirm an entry. 1 means require a 1% margin; 0 enters on a bare cross. | text | — | Raise it above 0 when the fast and slow EMAs are crossing back and forth and you are getting chopped up by false starts. | Requiring a margin means fewer entries, later. You give up the earliest part of a move in exchange for skipping crosses that immediately reverse. `0` takes every bare cross. |

**Entry Sizing**

| Setting | What it is | Values | Default | When to change it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `entrySizing.mode`<br/>Mode | Size each entry by a fixed quote amount or a percent of account equity. | `fixed`, `percentOfAccount` | `fixed` | Use `fixed` while you are learning what the strategy does — it makes every trade the same size and therefore easy to compare. Switch to `percentOfAccount` when you want position size to grow and shrink with the account. | In `fixed` mode only the amount field is read; in `percentOfAccount` mode only the percent field is. Setting the wrong one is the usual cause of "it never buys". |
| `entrySizing.amount`<br/>Amount | Quote-asset amount spent on each entry when sizing by fixed amount. | text | `""` | Only in `fixed` mode. Set it to what you are willing to put into one coin, and keep it above the exchange minimum order size for your pairs. | Every entry spends exactly this much quote currency. Below the exchange minimum the order is rejected and the entry silently never happens. |
| `entrySizing.percent`<br/>Percent | Percent of account equity spent on each entry. 10 means 10% of your cash plus the value of coins you hold. | text | `""` | Only in `percentOfAccount` mode. Start small — 5–10% — so a bad run cannot concentrate the account into one coin. | Position size scales with equity, so gains compound and losses shrink the next bet. Set high, a few simultaneous entries can commit most of the account. |

**Account Cap**

| Setting | What it is | Values | Default | When to change it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `accountCap.mode`<br/>Mode | Whether to cap how much of the account is deployed into coins at once. | `off`, `percentOfAccount` | `off` | Turn it on as soon as the profile trades more than one or two coins, so a strong signal across many coins cannot deploy the whole account at once. | `off` means no ceiling: the strategy will keep entering while signals fire. `percentOfAccount` refuses new entries once holdings reach the configured share of equity. |
| `accountCap.percent`<br/>Percent | Most of the account, by equity, to hold in coins at once. 50 keeps about half as a cash reserve. | text | `""` | Only when the cap mode is on. Pick the share of the account you are comfortable having in coins simultaneously. | New entries are blocked once holdings reach this share of equity; existing positions and their exits are unaffected. At `50` roughly half the account stays as cash. |

**EMA**

| Setting | What it is | Values | Default | When to change it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ema.fast`<br/>Fast EMA length (candles) | Fast EMA period, in candles. Must be shorter than the slow period. | number, min 1, max 9007199254740991 | _required_ | Set it with the slow period as a pair. Shorter reacts sooner and trades more. | The entry signal is the fast EMA crossing above the slow. A very short fast period produces frequent, noisy crosses; it must be shorter than the slow period or the config is rejected. |
| `ema.slow`<br/>Slow EMA length (candles) | Slow EMA period, in candles. Must be longer than the fast period. | number, min 2, max 9007199254740991 | _required_ | Set it with the fast period as a pair. A wider gap between the two means fewer, higher-conviction crosses. | Lengthening it delays both entry and the loss of the signal, so trades become fewer and longer. It must be longer than the fast period. |

**ATR Trailing Stop**

| Setting | What it is | Values | Default | When to change it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `atrTrailingStop.enabled`<br/>Enabled | Scale the trailing stop to the coin’s own volatility (ATR) instead of a fixed percent, so a volatile coin gets a wider stop and a calm one a tighter stop. Unlike the fixed percent, this stop can also move DOWN when volatility spikes (it is not a one-way ratchet), giving a volatile move room rather than shaking you out. | on / off | `false` | Turn it on when one fixed percentage does not suit every coin the profile trades — a stop that is right for a stablecoin pair is far too tight for a small-cap. | The stop distance follows the coin's own recent volatility instead of a fixed percent, and it replaces the fixed trailing stop. Unlike the fixed stop it can also move down when volatility spikes, which gives a violent move room instead of shaking you out. |
| `atrTrailingStop.period`<br/>Period | ATR lookback in candles, on the strategy candle interval. | number, min 2, max 100 | `14` | Only when the ATR stop is on. Shorten it to make the stop respond faster to a change in volatility. | A short period makes the stop jumpy as volatility changes; a long period smooths it but is slower to widen when a coin becomes volatile. |
| `atrTrailingStop.multiple`<br/>Multiple | How many ATRs below the peak the stop sits. 3 means sell when price falls 3 ATRs from the high reached since entry. | text | `3` | Only when the ATR stop is on. Raise it if normal volatility keeps stopping you out; lower it to protect gains harder. | The stop sits this many ATRs below the peak since entry. At `3` a coin whose ATR is 2% of price gets roughly a 6% pullback allowance, and that allowance moves as volatility does. |

**Protective Stop**

| Setting | What it is | Values | Default | When to change it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `protectiveStop.enabled`<br/>Enabled | Rest a STOP_LOSS_LIMIT on the exchange that tracks the trailing-stop level. | on / off | `false` | Turn it on if you want protection that survives the bot being offline. The in-memory trailing stop only fires while the worker is running. | A real stop order rests on Binance and tracks the trailing level, so a crash or restart cannot leave the position unprotected. The cost is an extra resting order and the usual stop-order risks in a gapping market. |
| `protectiveStop.limitOffsetPercentage`<br/>Limit Offset Percentage | Limit price as a fraction of the stop trigger (0.98 = 2% below). | text | `0.98` | Only when the protective stop is on. Lower it (further below the trigger) on thin, volatile coins where a stop can gap through a tight limit. | When the stop triggers, the limit is placed this fraction of the trigger price. At `0.98` the limit sits 2% below the trigger — wide enough to fill in most conditions. Too tight and the stop triggers but never fills, leaving you holding. |

**Trend Filter**

| Setting | What it is | Values | Default | When to change it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `trendFilter.enabled`<br/>Enabled | Only enter while price is above the long-term trend line, so the bot sits out confirmed downtrends instead of buying into them. Exits are unaffected. | on / off | `false` | Turn it on when backtests show the strategy losing money mainly on entries taken during sustained downtrends. | Entries are refused while price is below the long-term trend line. Exits are untouched, so you can still get out. Fewer trades overall, and you will sit out the early part of a recovery. |
| `trendFilter.maType`<br/>MA Type | Moving-average type for the long-term trend line. | `sma`, `ema` | `sma` | Only when the trend filter is on. `ema` weights recent prices more heavily, so it turns sooner than `sma`. | `ema` re-admits entries earlier after a downtrend ends, at the cost of more false re-entries. `sma` is slower and steadier. |
| `trendFilter.period`<br/>Period | Trend-line lookback in candles, on the strategy candle interval. 200 on a daily interval is the classic macro trend; a shorter period reacts faster. | number, min 2, max 400 | `200` | Only when the trend filter is on. Shorten it if the filter is blocking entries long after the market has clearly turned. | Measured in candles of your candle interval, so `200` is about 8 days on `1h` and 200 days on `1d`. A long period blocks a large share of entries; a short one barely filters anything. |
| `trendFilter.requireRising`<br/>Require Rising | Also require the trend line itself to be rising, not just price above it. This rejects entries on bear rallies that pop above a line that is still falling. Off keeps the simpler price-above-line gate. | on / off | `false` | Turn it on when you keep entering on rallies that pop above a trend line which is still heading down. | Both conditions must hold: price above the line, and the line itself higher than it was. Noticeably fewer entries, and later ones. Off keeps the simpler price-above-line test. |
| `trendFilter.slopeLookbackBars`<br/>Slope Lookback Bars | When "require rising" is on, how many candles back to measure the slope. The trend line must sit higher now than this many candles ago. Only used when "require rising" is on. | number, min 1, max 200 | `10` | Only when "require rising" is on. Shorten it to accept a trend line that has only just turned up; lengthen it to demand a sustained turn. | The line must be higher now than this many candles ago. A long lookback rejects entries for a long time after a downtrend, so a recovery is largely missed. |

**Entry Extension**

| Setting | What it is | Values | Default | When to change it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `entryExtension.enabled`<br/>Enabled | Skip an entry while price is stretched too far above its baseline trend line, so the bot does not buy into an overextended blow-off. Exits are unaffected. | on / off | `false` | Turn it on if you find the strategy buying at the top of vertical moves that immediately mean-revert. | Entries are skipped while price is stretched too far above its baseline, so you buy pullbacks rather than blow-offs. In a strong sustained trend this can keep you out for a long time. |
| `entryExtension.maType`<br/>MA Type | Moving-average type for the baseline the stretch is measured from. | `sma`, `ema` | `sma` | Only when entry extension is on. `ema` tracks price more closely, so "stretched" is measured against a faster-moving baseline. | `ema` follows a rising market up, so it blocks fewer entries in a steady trend. `sma` is a stiffer baseline and blocks more. |
| `entryExtension.period`<br/>Period | Baseline lookback in candles, on the strategy candle interval. 50 on a daily interval is a common medium-term baseline. | number, min 2, max 400 | `50` | Only when entry extension is on. Shorten it to compare against a more recent baseline. | Measured in candles of your candle interval. A short period makes the baseline chase price, so almost nothing looks stretched; a long one makes the check bite more often. |
| `entryExtension.maxPercent`<br/>Max Percent | How far above the baseline price may sit and still enter. 40 means skip an entry while price is more than 40% above the baseline line. | text | `0.4` | Only when entry extension is on. Lower it to be stricter about chasing; raise it if it is blocking entries you wanted. | Entries are skipped while price sits more than this far above the baseline. Set it too low on a volatile coin and virtually every entry is blocked. |
